edges.reason: Seven/eight/nine products can be built independently by equal groups; the earlier two-through-six fact table is useful preparation but not a logical requirement to learn those products.
The target explicitly distinguishes boundary length from area. Perimeter meaning is required for that contrast, not all rectangle/square perimeter computations.

The target must identify the base and corresponding height of a parallelogram, not merely multiply two labeled numbers. This uses the pair of parallel opposite sides that defines that shape and locates the opposite line. Restrict necessity to that meaning, without requiring all trapezoid properties or a rectangle derivation.
edges.scope: The parallelogram opposite-side meaning when identifying a base and its corresponding perpendicular height
